More farm produce exported to Mideast
Adrian Kenneth Halili - The Philippine Star
August 9, 2026 | 12:00am
In a statement, the DA said 17.2 MT of Cardava bananas, sweet potatoes and singkamas (turnip) had been shipped to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The country has expanded its agricultural export push in the Middle East following the shipment of more than 17 metric tons (MT) of Davao-grown produce to Saudi Arabia, according to the Department of Agriculture (DA).
In a statement, the DA said 17.2 MT of Cardava bananas, sweet potatoes and singkamas (turnip) had been shipped to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia.
The shipment had a total value of P800,000 and consisted of 1,350 boxes of bananas weighing 12 kilos each, 50 boxes of sweet potatoes and 50 boxes of singkamas, each weighing 10 kilos.
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said further expansion of the overseas market would allow the country to reduce its more than $11 billion annual farm trade deficit.
“Expanding agricultural exports helps narrow our trade deficit, encourages investments in modern farming and logistics, generates jobs in rural communities and builds a more competitive agricultural sector that can drive long-term economic growth,” he added.
Tiu Laurel said new export markets would create new opportunities for the country’s farmers to receive higher incomes, “instead of allowing that value to benefit producers in other countries.”
The produce was exported by Gerb Golden Hands Corp. from Sto. Tomas in Davao del Norte and bound for Jeddah-based Rana Mohammed Saleem Commercial LLC.
Davao Region executive director Macario Gonzaga said the recent shipment showed that continued export promotion could provide concrete results for the region’s farmers and agribusinesses.
He added that continued participation in international trade exhibitions creates marketing opportunities for local farmers and exporters.
“Every successful shipment strengthens Davao Region’s reputation as a dependable source of premium agricultural products and opens the door to more sustained export opportunities,” Gonzaga said.
Business discussions were held during the AGRA Middle East Exhibition held at the Dubai World Trade Centre in 2024, where the DA’s Agriculture Regional Field Office XI and Gerb Golden Hands showcased Davao’s agricultural products.

SA opens new trade route as first grape shipment lands in Philippines
29 March 2026
in News, Fruit, Global, South Africa
Reading Time: 4 mins read
Celebrating the arrival of the first shipment of South African grapes to the Philippines in Manilla on 26 March 2026. From left: Importer Kingson Chan; Diana Ang, merchandising director of The Marketplace and Shopwise Supermarket; Her Excellency Bartinah Ntombizodwa Radebe-Netshitenzhe, South African Ambassador to the Philippines; Mecia Petersen, CEO of the South African Table Grape Industry; and Johannes Mashaba, special adviser to the South African Minister of Agriculture. Photo: Supplied
South Africa has officially opened a new agricultural export corridor to Southeast Asia, with the first shipment of locally produced table grapes successfully arriving in the Philippines.
By Maile Matsimela, digital editor at African Farming
The milestone, confirmed by Minister of Agriculture John Steenhuisen, follows the granting of market access in 2025 and marks a significant breakthrough for the country’s fruit export sector.
A Breakthrough for Agricultural Trade
The inaugural shipment signals more than just a new destination for South African produce. It represents years of technical negotiations and collaboration between the South African and Philippine governments, as well as industry stakeholders.
According to Steenhuisen, the development underscores the importance of science-based phytosanitary standards and strong diplomatic ties in unlocking global markets.
“This is not just a commercial transaction, but the opening of a new trade corridor,” he said, highlighting the role of cooperation and trust in expanding agricultural trade.
Also read: From pineapple waste to global markets: Eastern Cape businesses step up export ambitions
A Lucrative and Growing Market
The Philippines presents a major opportunity for South African exporters. Ranked among the world’s top 20 importers of table grapes, the country imported an estimated 74 000 tonnes in 2024, equivalent to about 16 million cartons.
With a population exceeding 118 million people, alongside a growing middle class and rising urbanisation, demand for fresh produce is expected to increase steadily.
This positions South Africa well to establish a long-term presence in the market, particularly during its peak supply season.
Strong Performance at Home
The new export route comes at a time when South Africa’s table grape industry continues to show resilience and growth.
So far in the 2025/26 season, exports have reached 76.6 million cartons, which is a reflection of the sector’s ability to adapt to shifting global demand and maintain high production standards.
Also read: Large grain crop expected: SACOTA and Steenhuisen tackle agricultural export bottlenecks
Diversifying Beyond Traditional Markets
The government has emphasised that expanding into markets like the Philippines forms part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on traditional trading partners.
Southeast Asia is increasingly seen as a strategic growth region for South African agriculture.
“Our goal is not to replace existing markets but to broaden our footprint in a way that supports long-term growth and stability,” said Steenhuisen.
Building a Long-term Partnership
Beyond immediate trade gains, South Africa is positioning the Philippines as a strategic partner in food security and agricultural development.
The table grape industry is expected to focus on strengthening its foothold in the market over the next three to five years, with plans to expand volumes, diversify grape varieties and deepen market integration.
The success of the first shipment has been attributed to coordinated efforts between government and industry, including the South African Table Grape Industry (SATI), the Department of Agriculture and diplomatic missions.
Steenhuisen said the achievement lays “a strong foundation for deeper cooperation, expanded trade and shared prosperity” between the two nations.

Islamabad, Riyadh agree to boost Pakistani agriculture and food exports to $3B in 2 years
Agreement reached after talks between Saudi Arabia’s Agriculture Ministry and Pakistan’s Food Security Ministry in Islamabad
Aamir Latif
30 August 2026•Update: 30 August 2026
ISLAMABAD
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have have agreed to boost Pakistani agricultural and food exports to the oil-rich kingdom up to $3 billion within the next two years, a joint statement on Sunday.
According to the statement, shared by the prime minister’s office, the agreement was reached after talks between Saudi Arabia’s Agriculture Ministry and Pakistan’s Food Security Ministry, at the initiative of Premier Shehbaz Sharif.
The development comes after a Saudi delegation led by Environment, Water and Agriculture Minister Abdulrahman A. Alfadley visited Islamabad last week. The Pakistani side was led by National Food Security and Research Minister Rana Tanvir Hussain.  
Sharif also met the Saudi delegation and discussed potential areas of bilateral cooperation.
The two sides identified rice, red meat, fruits and fruit concentrates, green fodder and water-efficient agricultural technologies as priority areas for expanding trade and investment, particularly through cooperation with Saudi Arabia’s private sector.
Pakistan supplied about 169,000 tons of rice worth $163 million to Saudi Arabia in 2025. The Saudi side expressed interest in further increasing bilateral trade of rice.
The two sides also reviewed Pakistan’s annual exports of around 30,000 tons of red meat valued at approximately $167 million. The Saudi side expressed interest in gradually doubling its imports of Pakistani red meat.
Green fodder was also identified as a promising sector for expanding trade and establishing long-term supply partnerships.
The two sides reviewed investment proposals from Pakistan’s private sector in livestock, agri-food processing and the rice value chain, agreeing to maintain coordination to advance the projects.
Both countries reaffirmed their longstanding strategic and fraternal ties and highlighted the alignment between Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 food-security priorities and Pakistan’s agricultural export potential.
Islamabad and Riyadh have increased bilaterral defense and economic cooperation in recent years. The two countries signed a a strategic mutual defense agreement last year, and a Mecca Joint Defense Agreement along with Turkiye earlier this month.

Islamabad, Riyadh agree to boost Pakistani agriculture and food exports to $3B in 2 years
 0 Comments
August 30, 2026 at 4:06 pm
Pakistan national flag. [Photo by Matt King-ICC/ICC via Getty Images]
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to boost Pakistani agricultural and food exports to the oil-rich kingdom up to $3 billion within the next two years, a joint statement on Sunday, Anadolu reports.
According to the statement, shared by the prime minister’s office, the agreement was reached after talks between Saudi Arabia’s Agriculture Ministry and Pakistan’s Food Security Ministry, at the initiative of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
The development comes after a Saudi delegation led by Environment, Water and Agriculture Minister Abdulrahman A. Alfadley visited Islamabad last week. The Pakistani side was led by National Food Security and Research Minister Rana Tanvir Hussain.
Sharif also met the Saudi delegation and discussed potential areas of bilateral cooperation.
The two sides identified rice, red meat, fruits and fruit concentrates, green fodder and water-efficient agricultural technologies as priority areas for expanding trade and investment, particularly through cooperation with Saudi Arabia’s private sector.
Pakistan supplied about 169,000 tons of rice worth $163 million to Saudi Arabia in 2025. The Saudi side expressed interest in further increasing bilateral trade of rice.
READ: Pakistan, cricket, and the lunch break comedy of a nervous regime
The two sides also reviewed Pakistan’s annual exports of around 30,000 tons of red meat valued at approximately $167 million. The Saudi side expressed interest in gradually doubling its imports of Pakistani red meat.
Green fodder was also identified as a promising sector for expanding trade and establishing long-term supply partnerships.
The two sides reviewed investment proposals from Pakistan’s private sector in livestock, agri-food processing and the rice value chain, agreeing to maintain coordination to advance the projects.
Both countries reaffirmed their longstanding strategic and fraternal ties and highlighted the alignment between Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 food-security priorities and Pakistan’s agricultural export potential.
Islamabad and Riyadh have increased bilaterral defense and economic cooperation in recent years. The two countries signed a a strategic mutual defense agreement last year, and a Mecca Joint Defense Agreement along with Turkiye earlier this month.

South Korea's NOFI purchases 136,000 tons corn at tender, traders claim
Posted to Maritime Reporter on May 8, 2026
According to European traders, the leading South Korean animal feed manufacturer?Nonghyup Feed Inc. (NOFI) purchased an estimated 136,000 metric tonnes of animal feed corn in a 'international tender that sought up to 207,000 tons.
The corn was bought in two consignments totaling 68,000 tons. A third consignment weighing up to 69,000 tonnes was not believed to have been purchased.
The first consignment of corn was purchased from the trading house Mitsui. It was partly bought at a?outright cost and freight price (c&f), estimated at $269.94 per ton, and partly for a premium?of 213.68 U.S. Cents per bushel over Chicago's September 2026 contract. Both were subject to a surcharge of $1.75 per ton for port unloading.
First consignment to arrive in South Korea was aimed for?September 1st. The following are the shipping periods for various origins: U.S. Pacific Northwest coast between July 24 and?August 12, U.S. Gulf, between July 4 and?July 23, South America, between June 29 to July 18, South Africa, between July 14 and?August 2.
The second consignment, allegedly purchased from Cargill was partly bought at an estimated outright of $269.88 per ton c&f as well as at a premium 211.78 U.S. Cents a bushel over the Chicago corn contract for September 2026. Both had a $1.50 surcharge per ton for additional port unloading.
Second consignment to arrive in South Korea was aimed for around September 10. The following are the?shipment periods from various origins: from 'the U.S. Pacific Northwest Coast between August 2 and 21; from 'the U.S. Gulf Between July 13 and August 1; from South America between July 8 - July 27 and from South Africa between July 23 - August 11
The reports reflect the opinions of traders, and it is possible to estimate prices and volumes later. Michael Hogan, reporting from Hamburg and David Goodman editing the report)
(source: Reuters)
